newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CHINA SEEN OPENING BUILDING SOCIETY MARKET SOON.
newsitem.headline: CHINA SEEN OPENING BUILDING SOCIETY MARKET SOON.

text.p: China is likely to allow the foundation of building societies soon, opening a potentially vast market for investors, Germany's Bausparkasse Schwabish Hall AG (BSH) said on Tuesday.
"According to our unofficial information, the positive decision has already been made," BSH Chairman Horst Kleiner told a news conference.
Kleiner added that according to data from China's ministry of construction, China will need to build 300 million new houses in the next 20 to 25 years.
"It is an enormous country, a vast market," he added.
The Chinese market was a potential part of BSG's international expansion strategy, which also targets Croatia, Poland, Chile and Argentina, Kleiner said.

According to BSG's preliminary plans, the company will start its operations in China's Shanghai province, inhabited by 90 million people, as soon as the country opens its market to foreign investors, he added.

Vietnam and South Africa are showing interest in BSH's know-how, and the company is also taking part in preparations for housing savings systems in Russia, Byelorussia, the Ukraine and Romania, BSH said in a statement.
BSH will open its Hungarian building society unit, Fundamenta Rt in a few weeks, as soon as Hungary's banking watchdog gives its permission for its operations, BSH said.
Hungary introduced its building society law on January 1, 1997, and the first building societies are expected to receive permissions for operations in the near future.

Since 1992, BSH acquired an over 80 percent share in the building society market of Slovakia, and 45 percent in the Czech Republic, and targets 30 to 40 percent market share in Hungary, BSH and Fundamenta officials said.
BSH, Germany's largest building society, had a balance sheet total of 47.7 billion marks in 1996, the company said in a statement.
